name: alias
summary: Creates a shortcut for a command.
description: Shell builtin that links a short name to a longer command: alias ll='ls -alF' makes ll run ls -alF. There must be no spaces around the =. An alias only lasts for the session; to keep it, add the line to ~/.bashrc (or ~/.bash_aliases). unalias removes an alias, and \command runs the original command, ignoring the alias.

options.description: Prints every alias in a reusable form.

arguments.name: NAME='COMMAND'
arguments.description: Alias definition. With just a NAME, prints its definition; without an argument, lists every alias.

examples.explanation: ll will now show a detailed list, hidden files included.

examples.command: alias update='sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade'
examples.explanation: A shortcut for a full update.
Prints the definition of an alias. To make it permanent, add the alias line to ~/.bashrc then run source ~/.bashrc.
